An Informal Talk

Practical Thought about Practical Thought?关于实用思考的实用思考？

What I’m going to try to do today is to extend the remarks I made two years ago at the USC Business School. You were assigned a transcript of my USC talk. There’s nothing I said then that I wouldn’t repeat today. But I want to amplify what I said then.

今天我想做的，是进一步展开我两年前在南加州大学商学院（USC Business School）讲过的话。你们已经拿到了我那次南加大演讲的文字稿。我当时说的每一句话，今天都愿意再说一遍。但我想把当时说的内容再作一些扩充。

The title of my talk is “Practical Thought about Practical Thought?,” with a question mark at the end. In a long career, I have assimilated various ultrasimple general notions that I find helpful in solving problems. Five of these helpful notions I will now describe. After that, I will present to you a problem of extreme scale. Indeed, the problem will involve turning startup capital of $2 million into $2 trillion, a sum large enough to represent a practical achievement. Then, I will try to solve the problem, assisted by my helpful general notions. Following that, I will suggest that there are important educational implications in my demonstration. I will so finish because my objective is educational, my game today being a search for better methods of thought.

关于现实思维的现实思考？

我的演讲题目是《关于现实思维的现实思考？》——在结尾处带有一个问号。在漫长的职业生涯中，我吸纳了一些极其简单的普遍观念，我发现它们对解决问题很有帮助。现在我要讲述其中五个有用的观念。之后，我会向你们提出一个规模极其庞大的问题。事实上，这个问题是要把200万美元的创业资本变成2万亿美元，这个数额足够称得上一种现实成就。接着，我将借助这些有用的普遍观念，尝试去解决这个问题。在那之后，我会指出，我的论证蕴含着重要的教育意义。我以此收尾，因为我的目的是教育性的，今天的游戏就是寻找更好的思维方法。

The first helpful notion is that it is usually best to simplify problems by deciding big no-brainer questions first.

第一个有用的观念是：通常最好的做法是先解决那些显而易见的重大难题，从而把问题简化。

The second helpful notion mimics Galileo’s206Galileo GalileiGalileo Galilei (1564–1642) , born near Pisa, Italy, had early thoughts of joining a monastic order. Ultimately, though, his interests and education turned to mathematics and medicine, and he is credited with fundamental findings in pendulums, gravity, trajectories, and many other topics. He constructed the first astronomical telescope and used it to discover Jupiter’s satellites and the Milky Way. In 1633, he was brought before the Inquisition in Rome, placed under house arrest for the remainder of his life, and made to renounce his beliefs in solar-centric Copernican theory. Despite the trying circumstances, he continued work on his and mathematical demonstrations concerning the two new sciences and completed it in 1638. Smuggled out of Italy and published in Holland, the delineates most of Galileo’s contributions to physics.伽利略·伽利莱（Galileo Galilei，1564–1642 年）生于意大利比萨附近，早年曾想过加入修道会。但最终，他的兴趣和学业转向了数学和医学，并在摆、重力、轨迹等许多课题上都有奠基性的发现。他制造了第一架天文望远镜，用它发现了木星的卫星和银河系。1633 年，他在罗马被宗教裁判所审讯，余生被软禁，并被要求放弃他对哥白尼日心说的信仰。尽管处境艰难，他仍继续研究他的《关于两门新科学的对话与数学证明》，并于 1638 年完成。该书被偷运出意大利、在荷兰出版，阐述了伽利略对物理学的大部分贡献。 conclusion that scientific reality is often revealed only by math as if math was the language of God. Galileo’s attitude also works well in messy, practical life. Without numerical fluency, in the part of life most of us inhabit, you are like a one-legged man in an ass-kicking contest.

第二个有用的观念与伽利略（Galileo）的结论相似：科学的真实面貌往往只有借助数学才能揭示，仿佛数学是上帝的语言。伽利略的态度在混乱而现实的生活中同样管用。在我们大多数人所处的生活中，如果没有数字运算能力，你就像一个独腿人闯进了一场踢屁股比赛。

“Without numerical fluency, you are like a one-legged man in an ass-kicking contest.”没有数字功底，你就像斗踢大赛里独腿的人。

The third helpful notion is that it is not enough to think problems through forward. You must also think in reverse, much like the rustic who wanted to know where he was going to die so that he’d never go there. Indeed, many problems can’t be solved forward. And that is why the great algebraist Carl Jacobi so often said, “Invert, always invert,” and why the Pythagoreans207Pythagoras thought in reverse to prove that the square root of two was an irrational number.

第三个有用的观念是：仅仅正向地把问题想透是不够的，你还必须反向思考，就像那个乡下人，想知道自己会在哪里死，这样他就永远不去那里。事实上，许多问题无法靠正向思考解决。而这正是伟大的代数学家卡尔·雅各比（Carl Jacobi）常说「反过来想，总是反过来想」的原因，也是毕达哥拉斯学派通过逆向思考来证明2的平方根是无理数的原因。

The fourth helpful notion is that the best and most practical wisdom is elementary academic wisdom. But there is one extremely important qualification: You must think in a multidisciplinary manner. You must routinely use all the easy-to-learn concepts from the freshman course in every basic subject. Where elementary ideas will serve, your problem-solving must not be limited, as academia and many business bureaucracies are limited, by extreme balkanization into disciplines and subdisciplines, with strong taboos against any venture outside assigned territory. Instead, you must do your multidisciplinary thinking in accord with Ben Franklin’s prescription in Poor Richard:208Poor Richard’s AlmanackThe model for Poor Charlie’s Almanack is, of course, Ben Franklin’s Poor Richard’s Almanack . Franklin, as many know, was a polymath. Born in Boston and a leader of the American Revolution, he was a journalist, publisher, author, philanthropist, abolitionist, public servant, scientist, librarian, diplomat, and inventor. Using the pseudonym of “Poor Richard,” Franklin published his Almanack from 1733 to 1758. Its content varied, including not only many Franklin aphorisms that became famous but also calendars, weather forecasts, astronomical information, and astrological data. The was hugely popular in the American colonies, selling about 10,000 copies a year.《穷查理宝典》的范本，当然就是本·富兰克林（Ben Franklin）的《穷理查年鉴》（Poor Richard's Almanack）。众所周知，富兰克林是位博学者，生于波士顿，是美国革命的领袖，也是记者、出版人、作家、慈善家、废奴主义者、公职人员、科学家、图书馆事业推动者、外交官和发明家。富兰克林以“穷理查”为笔名，从 1733 年到 1758 年出版他的年鉴。内容多样，不仅有众多后来广为人知的富兰克林格言，还有日历、天气预报、天文信息和占星数据。《穷理查年鉴》在美洲殖民地大受欢迎，每年售出约一万册。 “If you want it done, go. If not, send.”

第四个有用的观念是：最好、最实用的智慧是基础的学术智慧。但有一个极其重要的前提：你必须以跨学科的方式思考。你必须经常运用每一门基础学科大一课程里那些易于学习的概念。在基础观念就够用的时候，你解决问题的方式绝不能被局限——正如学术界和许多商业官僚机构那样，被学科与亚学科之间极度的割裂所束缚，并且对任何越出指定领地的举动都怀有强烈的禁忌。相反，你必须依照本杰明·富兰克林（Ben Franklin）在《穷理查年鉴208Poor Richard’s AlmanackThe model for Poor Charlie’s Almanack is, of course, Ben Franklin’s Poor Richard’s Almanack . Franklin, as many know, was a polymath. Born in Boston and a leader of the American Revolution, he was a journalist, publisher, author, philanthropist, abolitionist, public servant, scientist, librarian, diplomat, and inventor. Using the pseudonym of “Poor Richard,” Franklin published his Almanack from 1733 to 1758. Its content varied, including not only many Franklin aphorisms that became famous but also calendars, weather forecasts, astronomical information, and astrological data. The was hugely popular in the American colonies, selling about 10,000 copies a year.《穷查理宝典》的范本，当然就是本·富兰克林（Ben Franklin）的《穷理查年鉴》（Poor Richard's Almanack）。众所周知，富兰克林是位博学者，生于波士顿，是美国革命的领袖，也是记者、出版人、作家、慈善家、废奴主义者、公职人员、科学家、图书馆事业推动者、外交官和发明家。富兰克林以“穷理查”为笔名，从 1733 年到 1758 年出版他的年鉴。内容多样，不仅有众多后来广为人知的富兰克林格言，还有日历、天气预报、天文信息和占星数据。《穷理查年鉴》在美洲殖民地大受欢迎，每年售出约一万册。》（Poor Richard）中的箴言来做跨学科思考：「如果你想要做成，就亲自去；如果不想，就派人去。」

If, in your thinking, you rely entirely on others, often through purchase of professional advice—whenever outside a small territory of your own—you will suffer much calamity. And it is not just difficulties in complex coordination that will do you in. You will also suffer from the reality evoked by the Shavian character who said, “In the last analysis, every profession is a conspiracy against the laity.”

如果在思考时你完全依赖他人——往往是通过购买专业建议——只要一超出你自己那小小的领地，你就会遭遇许多灾难。把你毁掉的，不只是复杂协调中的种种困难。你还会受困于萧伯纳（Shaw）笔下那个人物所道出的现实，他说：「说到底，每一种职业都是一场针对外行人的共谋。」

Indeed, a Shavian character, for once, understated the horrors of something [Geroge Bernard] Shaw didn’t like. It is not usually the conscious malfeasance of your narrow professional adviser that does you in. Instead, your troubles come from his subconscious bias. His cognition will often be impaired, for your purposes, by financial incentives different from yours. And he will also suffer from the psychological defect caught by the proverb “To a man with a hammer, every problem looks like a nail.”

通常把你毁掉的并不是你那位眼界狭窄的专业顾问有意识的恶意行为。相反，你的麻烦来自他的潜意识偏见。

“It is not usually the conscious malfeasance of your narrow professional adviser that does you in. Instead, your troubles come from his subconscious bias.”把你拖垮的，通常不是你那位狭隘的专业顾问有意识的恶意。相反，你的麻烦来自他潜意识的偏见。

The fifth helpful notion is that really big effects, lollapalooza effects, will often come only from large combinations of factors. For instance, tuberculosis was tamed, at least for a long time, only by routine, combined use in each case of three different drugs. And other lollapalooza effects, like the flight of an airplane,206flight of an airplane飞机飞行 follow a similar pattern.

第五个有用的观念是：真正巨大的效应，即 lollapalooza 效应（多重因素合力造成的超级效应），往往只有靠大量因素的组合才会出现。例如，结核病之所以能被制服——至少长期如此——靠的是在每一病例中常规性地联合使用三种不同的药物。其他的 lollapalooza 效应，比如飞机的飞行，206flight of an airplane飞机飞行也遵循类似的模式。

It is now time to present my practical problem. And here is the problem:

现在是时候提出我的现实问题了。问题如下：

It is 1884 in Atlanta. You are brought, along with 20 others like you, before a rich and eccentric Atlanta citizen named Glotz. Both you and Glotz share two characteristics: her of First, you routinely use in problem-solving the five helpful notions, and second, you know all the elementary ideas in all the basic college courses, as taught in 1996. However, all discoverers and all examples demonstrating these elementary ideas come from dates before 1884. Neither you nor Glotz knows anything about anything that has happened after 1884.211Coca-cola可口可乐

时间是1884年的亚特兰大。你和另外20个与你相似的人，被带到一位富有而古怪的亚特兰大市民格罗兹（Glotz）面前。你和格罗兹有两个共同点：第一，你在解决问题时会常规性地运用那五个有用的观念；第二，你掌握了1996年所讲授的所有基础大学课程中的所有基础观念。然而，所有这些观念的发现者以及佐证这些观念的例证，都来自1884年之前。你和格罗兹对1884年之后发生的任何事情都一无所知。

Glotz offers to invest $2 million in 1884 dollars, yet take only half the equity, for a Glotz Charitable Foundation, in a new corporation organized to go into the non-alcoholic beverage business and remain in that business only, forever. Glotz wants to use a name that has somehow charmed him: Coca-Cola.

格罗兹愿意投入200万美元（按1884年币值），却只拿走一半的股权，用于一个格罗兹慈善基金会，投入一家新成立、专营且永远只经营非酒精饮料业务的新公司。格罗兹想用一个莫名令他着迷的名字：可口可乐211Coca-cola可口可乐（Coca-Cola）。

The other half of the new corporation’s equity will go to the man who most plausibly demonstrates that his business plan will cause Glotz’s foundation to be worth a trillion dollars 150 years later, in the money of that later time, 2034, despite paying out a large part of its earnings each year as a dividend. This will make the whole new corporation worth $2 trillion, even after paying out many billions of dollars in dividends.

新公司的另一半股权，将归那个最能令人信服地证明以下一点的人：他的商业计划能让格罗兹的基金在150年后的2034年（按当时货币计）价值达到一万亿美元，尽管每年都把大部分盈利作为股息派发。这将使整个新公司的价值达到2万亿美元，即便在派发了数百亿美元的股息之后依然如此。

You have 15 minutes to make your pitch. What do you say to Glotz?

你有15分钟时间来做陈述。你会对格罗兹说些什么？

Here is my solution, my pitch to Glotz, using only the helpful notions and what every bright college sophomore should know:

下面是我的解决方案，即我对格罗兹的陈词，只运用了那些有用的观念，以及每个聪明的大学二年级学生都该知道的东西：

Well, Glotz, the big no-brainer decisions that, to simplify our problem, should be made first are as follows: First, we are never going to create something worth $2 trillion by selling some generic beverage. Therefore, we must make your name, Coca-Cola, into a strong, legally protected trademark.212TrademarkA name, symbol, or other device identifying a product, officially registered and legally restricted to the use of the owner or manufacturer. A distinctive characteristic by which a person or thing comes to be known.商标：用以识别某产品、经正式注册并依法专属于所有者或制造商使用的名称、符号或其他装置。也指一个人或事物赖以被人知晓的鲜明特征。 Second, we can get to $2 trillion only by starting in Atlanta, then succeeding in the rest of the United States, then rapidly succeeding with our new beverage all over the world. This will require developing a product that has universal appeal because it harnesses powerful elemental forces. And the right place to find such powerful elemental forces is in the subject matter of elementary academic courses.

好吧，格罗兹，为了把问题简化，应当最先做出的那些显而易见的重大决定如下：第一，我们绝不可能靠卖某种无品牌的饮料，创造出价值2万亿美元的东西。因此，我们必须把你的名字「可口可乐」变成一个强大、受法律保护的商标。第二，我们只有先在亚特兰大起步，接着在美国其他地方取得成功，然后迅速让我们的新饮料风靡全世界，才能达到2万亿美元。这需要我们开发出一种具有普遍吸引力的产品，因为它要驾驭强大的基本力量。而寻找这种强大基本力量的正确之地，就在基础学术课程的学科内容之中。

Coca-Cola, all over the world

We will next use numerical fluency to ascertain what our target implies. We can guess reasonably that by 2034 there will be about 8 billion beverage consumers in the world. On average, each of these consumers will be much more prosperous in real terms than the average consumer of 1884. Each consumer is composed mostly of water and must ingest about 64 ounces of water per day. This is eight 8-ounce servings. Thus, if our new beverage, and other imitative beverages in our new market, can flavor and otherwise improve only 25 percent of ingested water worldwide, and we can occupy half of the new world market, we can sell 2.92 trillion 8-ounce servings in 2034. And if we can then net 4xa2 per serving, we will earn $117 billion. This will be enough, if our business is still growing at a good rate, to make it easily worth $2 trillion.

接下来我们将运用数字运算能力，来确定我们的目标意味着什么。我们可以合理地推测，到2034年，全世界将约有80亿饮料消费者。平均而言，这些消费者中的每一个，其实际生活水平都将远高于1884年的平均消费者。每个消费者主要由水构成，每天必须摄入约64盎司的水。这就是八份8盎司的量。因此，如果我们的新饮料，以及我们新市场上其他模仿性的饮料，能够仅仅为全世界摄入水分的25%增添风味并作其他改良，而我们能占据新世界市场的一半，那么到2034年我们就能卖出2.92万亿份8盎司的饮料。如果我们每份能净赚4美分，我们将赚得1170亿美元。只要我们的业务仍以良好的速度增长，这就足以让它轻而易举地价值2万亿美元。

A big question, of course, is whether 4xa2 per serving is a reasonable profit target for 2034. And the answer is yes if we can create a beverage with strong universal appeal. One hundred and fifty years is a long time. The dollar, like the Roman drachma,214Roman drachmaThe was originally a unit of currency in classical Greece. The word derives from the verb “to grasp.” The drachma was also used in ancient Rome in the third century BC and later. Most historians say one Roman drachma was equivalent to a day’s wages for a laborer.德拉克马（drachma）最初是古典希腊的一种货币单位。该词源自意为“抓取”的动词。德拉克马在公元前三世纪及以后的古罗马也有使用。多数史学家认为，一个罗马德拉克马相当于一名劳工一天的工资。 will almost surely suffer monetary depreciation. Concurrently, real purchasing power of the average beverage consumer in the world will go way up. His proclivity to inexpensively improve his experience while ingesting water will go up considerably faster. Meanwhile, as technology improves, the cost of our simple product, in units of constant purchasing power, will go down. All four factors will work together in favor of our 4xa2 per-serving profit target. Worldwide beverage purchasing power in dollars will probably multiply by a factor of at least 40 over 150 years. Thinking in reverse, this makes our profit-per-serving target, under 1884 conditions, a mere one-fortieth of 4xa2 or one-tenth of a cent per serving. This is an easy-to-exceed target as we start out if our new product has universal appeal.

当然，一个大问题是，每份4美分对于2034年来说是不是一个合理的利润目标。答案是肯定的——只要我们能够创造出一种具有强烈普遍吸引力的饮料。150年是一段很长的时间。美元，就像罗马的德拉克马214Roman drachmaThe was originally a unit of currency in classical Greece. The word derives from the verb “to grasp.” The drachma was also used in ancient Rome in the third century BC and later. Most historians say one Roman drachma was equivalent to a day’s wages for a laborer.德拉克马（drachma）最初是古典希腊的一种货币单位。该词源自意为“抓取”的动词。德拉克马在公元前三世纪及以后的古罗马也有使用。多数史学家认为，一个罗马德拉克马相当于一名劳工一天的工资。（drachma），几乎肯定会遭遇货币贬值。与此同时，全世界普通饮料消费者的实际购买力将大幅上升。他以低廉代价改善饮水体验的倾向，上升得还要快得多。同时，随着技术进步，我们这种简单产品以不变购买力计的成本将会下降。所有这四个因素会共同发力，支持我们每份4美分的利润目标。全世界的饮料购买力（以美元计）在150年间可能会增加至少40倍。倒过来想，这就意味着在1884年的条件下，我们每份的利润目标仅仅相当于4美分的四十分之一，即每份十分之一美分。如果我们的新产品具有普遍吸引力，这在我们起步时是一个极易超越的目标。

That decided, we must next solve the problem of invention to create universal appeal. There are two intertwined challenges of large scale. First, over 150 years, we must cause a new-beverage market to assimilate about one-fourth of the world’s water ingestion. Second, we must so operate that half the new market is ours while all our competitors combined are left to share the remaining half. These results are lollapalooza results. Accordingly, we must attack our problem by causing every favorable factor we can think of to work for us. Plainly, only a powerful combination of many factors is likely to cause the lollapalooza consequences we desire. Fortunately, the solution to these intertwined problems turns out to be fairly easy if one has stayed awake in all the freshman courses.

既然这一点已经确定，接下来我们必须解决发明的问题，以创造普遍吸引力。这里有两道相互交织的大规模挑战。第一，在150年间，我们必须让一个新的饮料市场吸纳全世界约四分之一的水分摄入。第二，我们必须如此经营，使得新市场的一半归我们，而我们所有竞争对手加在一起只能分掉剩下的另一半。这些结果都是 lollapalooza 效应式的结果。因此，我们必须让每一个能想到的有利因素都为我们所用，从而攻克这个难题。显然，只有许多因素的强大组合，才有可能引发我们想要的 lollapalooza 后果。幸运的是，如果一个人上大一课程时没有打瞌睡，这些交织问题的解法其实是相当容易的。

Let us start by exploring the consequences of our simplifying no-brainer decision that we must rely on a strong trademark. This conclusion automatically leads to an understanding of the essence of our business in proper elementary academic terms. We can see from the introductory course in psychology that, in essence, we are going into the business of creating and maintaining conditioned reflexes. The Coca-Cola trade name and trade dress will act as the stimuli, and the purchase and ingestion of our beverage will be the desired responses.

让我们从探究那个简化性的重大决定——我们必须依赖一个强大的商标——所带来的一切后果开始。这个结论会自动引导我们用恰当的基础学术术语来理解我们生意的本质。从心理学导论课中我们可以看到，本质上，我们要从事的是一门创造并维持条件反射的生意。「可口可乐」的商标名称和商标形象将充当刺激物，而对我们饮料的购买与饮用则是我们想要的反应。

本质上，我们要从事的是一门创造并维持条件反射的生意。

“In essence, we are going into the business of creating and maintaining conditioned reflexes.”本质上，我们要做的生意，是创造并维持条件反射。

And how does one create and maintain conditioned reflexes? Well, the psychology text gives two answers: 1) by operant conditioning and 2) by classical conditioning, often called Pavlovian215PavlovianIvan Pavlov (1849–1936) was born in central Russia and attended seminary until age 21, when he abandoned theology in favor of chemistry and physiology. Earning his MD in 1883, he excelled in physiology and surgical techniques. Later, he studied the secretory activity of digestion and ultimately formulated the laws of conditioned reflexes. Pavlov’s most famous experiment showed that dogs tend to salivate before food is actually delivered to their mouths. This result led him to a long series of experiments in which he manipulated the stimuli occurring before the presentation of food. He thereby established the basic laws for the establishment and extinction of what he called “conditional reflexes,” later mistranslated from the original Russian as “conditioned reflexes.” He was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1904 for his work on digestive secretions.伊万·巴甫洛夫（Ivan Pavlov，1849–1936 年）生于俄罗斯中部，在神学院读到 21 岁，随后弃神学而选化学和生理学。1883 年他获得医学博士学位，在生理学和外科手术技艺上表现出色。后来，他研究消化液的分泌活动，最终归纳出条件反射的规律。巴甫洛夫最著名的实验表明，狗在食物真正送到嘴边之前就会开始分泌唾液。这一结果引导他进行了一长串实验，在实验中他操控食物呈现之前发生的刺激，从而为他所谓的“条件反射”（conditional reflexes，该词后来由俄语原意误译为 conditioned reflexes）的建立与消退确立了基本规律。1904 年，他因消化液研究获诺贝尔奖。 conditioning to honor the great Russian scientist. And since we want a lollapalooza result, we must use both conditioning techniques, and all we can invent to enhance effects from each technique.

那么，人是如何创造并维持条件反射的呢？心理学教科书给出了两个答案：一、通过操作性条件反射；二、通过经典条件反射，通常被称为巴甫洛夫215PavlovianIvan Pavlov (1849–1936) was born in central Russia and attended seminary until age 21, when he abandoned theology in favor of chemistry and physiology. Earning his MD in 1883, he excelled in physiology and surgical techniques. Later, he studied the secretory activity of digestion and ultimately formulated the laws of conditioned reflexes. Pavlov’s most famous experiment showed that dogs tend to salivate before food is actually delivered to their mouths. This result led him to a long series of experiments in which he manipulated the stimuli occurring before the presentation of food. He thereby established the basic laws for the establishment and extinction of what he called “conditional reflexes,” later mistranslated from the original Russian as “conditioned reflexes.” He was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1904 for his work on digestive secretions.伊万·巴甫洛夫（Ivan Pavlov，1849–1936 年）生于俄罗斯中部，在神学院读到 21 岁，随后弃神学而选化学和生理学。1883 年他获得医学博士学位，在生理学和外科手术技艺上表现出色。后来，他研究消化液的分泌活动，最终归纳出条件反射的规律。巴甫洛夫最著名的实验表明，狗在食物真正送到嘴边之前就会开始分泌唾液。这一结果引导他进行了一长串实验，在实验中他操控食物呈现之前发生的刺激，从而为他所谓的“条件反射”（conditional reflexes，该词后来由俄语原意误译为 conditioned reflexes）的建立与消退确立了基本规律。1904 年，他因消化液研究获诺贝尔奖。（Pavlov）条件反射，以纪念这位伟大的俄罗斯科学家。既然我们想要一个 lollapalooza 效应式的结果，我们就必须同时运用这两种条件反射技术——以及我们所能发明出来、用以增强每一种技术效果的一切手段。

The operant conditioning part of our problem is easy to solve. We need only 1) maximize rewards of our beverage’s ingestion and 2) minimize possibilities that desired reflexes, once created by us, will be extinguished through operant conditioning by proprietors of competing products.

我们的问题中操作性条件反射的部分很容易解决。我们只需要：一、将饮用我们饮料所带来的回报最大化；二、把这样一种可能性降到最低——即我们一旦创造出想要的条件反射，便被竞争产品所有者通过操作性条件反射而将其消除。

For operant conditioning rewards, there are only a few categories we will find practical:

就操作性条件反射的回报而言，我们发现现实可行的只有寥寥几类：

01Food value in calories or other inputs
02Flavor, texture, and aroma acting as stimuli to consumption under neural preprogramming of man through Darwinian natural selection

Darwinian natural selection

达尔文的自然选择

03Stimulus, as by sugar or caffeine
04Cooling effect when man is too hot or warming effect when man is too cool

Wanting a lollapalooza result, we will naturally include rewards in all the categories.

既然想要一个 lollapalooza 效应式的结果，我们自然会把这几类回报全部纳入。

To start out, it is easy to decide to design our beverage for consumption cold. There is much less opportunity, without ingesting a beverage, to counteract excessive heat compared with excessive cold. Moreover, with excessive heat, much liquid must be consumed, and the reverse is not true.

首先，我们很容易决定把饮料设计成冷饮。与过热相比，在不摄入饮料的情况下，对抗过冷的机会要小得多。而且，在过热时，必须摄入大量液体，反过来则不成立。

It is also easy to decide to include both sugar and caffeine. After all, tea, coffee, and lemonade are already widely consumed. And it is also clear that we must be fanatic about determining, through trial and error, flavor and other characteristics that will maximize human pleasure while taking in the sugared water and caffeine we will provide.

同样容易决定的是同时加入糖和咖啡因。毕竟，茶、咖啡和柠檬水早已被广泛饮用。而且同样清楚的是，我们必须狂热地通过反复试验，来确定那些能在人们摄入我们所提供的含糖水和咖啡因时，使人的愉悦感最大化的风味及其他特性。

And, to counteract possibilities that desired operant-conditioned reflexes, once created by us, will be extinguished by operant-conditioning-employing competing products, there is also an obvious answer: We will make it a permanent obsession in our company that our beverage, as fast as practicable, will at all times be available everywhere throughout the world. After all, a competing product, if it is never tried, can’t act as a reward creating a conflicting habit. Every spouse knows that.

再者，为了抵消这样一种可能性——即我们一旦创造出的、由操作性条件反射形成的想要反射，会被采用操作性条件反射的竞争产品所消除——答案也很明显：我们要让「我们的饮料在切实可行的速度下，随时随地供应全世界」成为公司永久的执念。毕竟，一种竞争产品如果从未被尝试过，就不可能作为一种回报去制造一种相互冲突的习惯。每个结了婚的人都懂这个道理。

一种竞争产品，如果从未被人尝试过，就不可能作为一种回报去制造相互冲突的习惯。每个结了婚的人都懂这个道理。

TEA, COFFEE, AND LEMONADE
“A competing product, if it is never tried, can’t act as a reward creating a conflicting habit. Every spouse knows that.”一款竞争产品，若从未被人试用，便无法作为奖赏去养成一种相抵触的习惯。这点每个配偶都懂。

We must next consider the Pavlovian conditioning we must also use. In Pavlovian conditioning, powerful effects come from mere association. The neural system of Pavlov’s dog218Pavlov’s dog巴甫洛夫的狗 causes it to salivate at the bell it can’t eat. And the brain of man yearns for the type of beverage held by the pretty woman he can’t have. And so, Glotz, we must use every sort of decent, honorable Pavlovian conditioning we can think of. For as long as we are in business, our beverage and its promotion must be associated in consumer minds with all other things consumers like or admire.

接下来我们必须考虑我们同样必须使用的巴甫洛夫条件反射。在巴甫洛夫条件反射中，仅凭联想就能产生强大的效应。巴甫洛夫那只狗的神经系统会让它在听到那只吃不到的铃铛时流口水。而男人的大脑会渴望那个他得不到的漂亮女人手中拿着的那种饮料。所以，格罗兹，我们必须运用每一种我们能想到的体面而正当的巴甫洛夫条件反射。只要我们在经营，我们的饮料及其推广就必须在消费者的心目中，与消费者所喜爱或钦佩的一切事物联系起来。

Such extensive Pavlovian conditioning will cost a lot of money, particularly for advertising.219Advertising广告 We will spend big money as far ahead as we can imagine. But the money will be effectively spent. As we expand fast in our new-beverage market, our competitors will face gross disadvantages of scale in buying advertising to create the Pavlovian conditioning they need. And this outcome, along with other volume-creates-power effects, should help us gain and hold at least 50 percent of the new market everywhere. Indeed, provided buyers are scattered, our higher volumes will give us very extreme cost advantages in distribution.

如此大规模的巴甫洛夫条件反射会耗费巨额资金，尤其是广告219Advertising广告费。我们将尽我们所想地向前看，花下大笔金钱。但这些钱会花得有效。随着我们在新饮料市场上迅速扩张，我们的竞争对手在购买广告以创造它们所需的巴甫洛夫条件反射时，将面临严重的规模劣势。这一结果，连同其他「销量创造力量」的效应，应当能帮助我们赢得并在各地保有新市场至少50%的份额。事实上，只要买家分散，我们更高的销量就会在分销上给我们带来极为极端的成本优势。

Moreover, Pavlovian effects from mere association will help us choose the flavor, texture, and color of our new beverage. Considering Pavlovian effects, we will have wisely chosen the exotic and expensive-sounding name “Coca-Cola” instead of a pedestrian name like “Glotz’s Sugared, Caffeinated Water.” For similar Pavlovian reasons, it will be wise to have our beverage look pretty much like wine instead of sugared water. So we will artificially color our beverage if it comes out clear. And we will carbonate our water, making our product seem like champagne, or some other expensive beverage, while also making its flavor better and imitation harder to arrange for competing products. And, because we are going to attach so many expensive psychological effects to our flavor, that flavor should be different from any other standard flavor so that we maximize difficulties for competitors and give no accidental same-flavor benefit to any existing product.

此外，仅凭联想产生的巴甫洛夫效应，会帮助我们选择新饮料的风味、口感和颜色。考虑到巴甫洛夫效应，我们当初明智地选择了「可口可乐」这个听起来异域而昂贵的名字，而不是像「格罗兹的含糖含咖啡因的水」这样平庸的名字。出于类似的巴甫洛夫式理由，让饮料看起来很像葡萄酒而非糖水，将是明智之举。因此，如果饮料天然是透明的，我们就要给它人工着色。我们还要给水中充入二氧化碳，使我们的产品看起来像香槟或其他昂贵的饮料，同时让它风味更佳，也让竞争产品更难模仿。而且，由于我们打算把那么多昂贵的心理效应附着在我们的风味上，这种风味就应不同于任何其他标准风味，从而让我们把竞争对手的困难最大化，并且不给任何现有产品带来意外的同味好处。

What else from the psychology textbook can help our new business? Well, there is that powerful “monkey see, monkey do”220Monkey see, monkey do猴子看，猴子做（模仿） aspect of human nature that psychologists often call social proof. Social proof—imitative consumption triggered by mere sight of consumption—will not only help induce trial of our beverage, it will also bolster perceived rewards from consumption. We will always take this powerful social proof factor into account as we design advertising and sales promotion and as we forego present profit to enhance present and future consumption. More than with most other products, increased selling power will come from each increase in sales.

心理学教科书还能为我们的新事业提供什么帮助？嗯，人性中有一种强大的「猴子看、猴子做」的面向，心理学家常称之为「社会认同」（social proof）。社会认同，即仅仅由于看到别人消费而触发的模仿性消费，不仅有助于诱使人们尝试我们的饮料，还会增强消费所带来的被感知的回报。我们在设计广告和促销、在放弃当前利润以提升当前及未来消费时，将永远把这种强大的社会认同因素考虑在内。与大多数其他产品相比，我们的每一次销量增长，都会带来更大的销售力量。

We can now see, Glotz, that by combining 1) much Pavlovian conditioning, 2) powerful social proof effects, and 3) a wonderful-tasting, energy-giving, stimulating, and desirably cold beverage that causes much operant conditioning, we are going to get sales that speed up for a long time by reason of the huge mixture of factors we have chosen. Therefore, we are going to start something like an autocatalytic reaction221Autocatalytic reactionAn autocatalytic reaction (also called autocatalysis) occurs when a single chemical reaction product is itself the catalyst for that reaction. For example, tin pest is an autocatalytic reaction of the element tin; at low temperatures, it causes deterioration of tin objects. Atmospheric ozone depletion is another example of an autocatalytic reaction.自催化反应（autocatalytic reaction，亦称 autocatalysis）发生在某一化学反应的产物本身就是该反应的催化剂之时。例如，锡疫就是元素锡的自催化反应；在低温下，它会导致锡器劣化。大气臭氧损耗是自催化反应的另一个例子。 in chemistry—precisely the sort of multifactor-triggered lollapalooza effect we need.

格罗兹，我们现在可以看到：通过将（一）大量巴甫洛夫条件反射、（二）强大的社会认同效应，以及（三）一种美味、提神、刺激且宜冷饮、并能引发大量操作性条件反射的饮料结合起来，由于我们选中的巨大因素混合物，我们的销量将在很长一段时间内加速增长。因此，我们将启动类似于化学中自催化反应221Autocatalytic reactionAn autocatalytic reaction (also called autocatalysis) occurs when a single chemical reaction product is itself the catalyst for that reaction. For example, tin pest is an autocatalytic reaction of the element tin; at low temperatures, it causes deterioration of tin objects. Atmospheric ozone depletion is another example of an autocatalytic reaction.自催化反应（autocatalytic reaction，亦称 autocatalysis）发生在某一化学反应的产物本身就是该反应的催化剂之时。例如，锡疫就是元素锡的自催化反应；在低温下，它会导致锡器劣化。大气臭氧损耗是自催化反应的另一个例子。的东西——恰恰就是我们所需要的那种由多因素触发的 lollapalooza 效应。

“We are going to start something like an autocatalytic reaction—precisely the sort of multifactor-triggered lollapalooza effect we need.”222Coca-cola bottle可口可乐瓶我们要启动的，类似于一种自催化反应——正是我们所需要的那种多因素触发的合力效应（lollapalooza）。

The logistics and the distribution strategy of our business will be simple. There are only two practical ways to sell our beverage: 1) as syrup223Coca-cola syrup可口可乐糖浆 to fountains224Coca-cola fountains可口可乐喷泉机 and restaurants and 2) as a complete carbonated water product in containers. Wanting lollapalooza results, we will naturally do it both ways. And, wanting huge Pavlovian and social proof effects, we will always spend on advertising and sales promotion, per serving, over 40 percent of the fountain price for syrup needed to make the serving.

我们生意的物流和分销策略将会很简单。销售我们的饮料，实际可行的办法只有两种：一、作为糖浆223Coca-cola syrup可口可乐糖浆卖给冷饮店和餐厅；二、作为装在容器中的完整碳酸水产品。既然想要 lollapalooza 效应式的结果，我们自然两种方式都会采用。而且，既然想要巨大的巴甫洛夫和社会认同效应，我们将始终在广告和促销上投入——每份所需的制作糖浆，其冷饮店售价的40%以上都花在广告和促销上。

A few syrup-making plants can serve the world. However, to avoid needless shipping of mere space and water, we will need many bottling plants scattered over the world. We will maximize profits if, like early General Electric with light bulbs, we always set the first-sale price, either 1) for fountain syrup or 2) for any container of our complete product. The best way to arrange this desirable profit-maximizing control is to make any independent bottler we need a subcontractor, not a vendee of syrup, and certainly not a vendee of syrup under a perpetual franchise specifying a syrup price frozen forever at its starting level.

少数几家糖浆厂就能供应全世界。然而，为了避免徒劳地运输空容器和水分，我们将需要在世界各地散布许多装瓶厂。如果我们像早期的通用电气（General Electric）对待灯泡那样，始终设定首次销售价格——无论是对冷饮店用的糖浆，还是对我们完整产品的任何容器——我们就能使利润最大化。安排这种理想的可使利润最大化的控制权的最佳方式，是把我们所需要的任何独立装瓶商变为分包商，而非糖浆的买主，当然更不是那种在永久特许经营下、按永远冻结在初始水平的糖浆价格购买糖浆的买主。

Being unable to get a patent or copyright on our super-important flavor, we will work obsessively to keep our formula secret. We will make a big hoopla over our secrecy, which will enhance Pavlovian effects. Eventually, food chemical engineering will advance so that our flavor can be copied with near exactitude. But by that time, we will be so far ahead, with such strong trademarks and complete, “always available” worldwide distribution, that good flavor copying won’t bar us from our objective. Moreover, the advances in food chemistry that help competitors will almost surely be accompanied by technological advances that will help us, including refrigeration, better transportation, and, for dieters, the ability to insert a sugar taste without inserting sugar’s calories. Also, there will be related beverage opportunities we will seize.

由于我们无法为这至关重要的风味申请专利或版权，我们将执着地努力保守配方秘密。我们要为保密大造声势，这会增强巴甫洛夫效应。最终，食品化学工程会进步到几乎能精确复制我们的风味。但到那时，我们已经遥遥领先，拥有如此强大的商标和完整、「永远可得」的全球分销网络，以至于出色的风味复制也无法阻挡我们实现目标。而且，帮助竞争对手的食品化学进步，几乎肯定会伴随帮助我们的技术进步，包括制冷、更好的运输，以及——对节食者而言——在不摄入糖的卡路里的情况下植入糖的味道的能力。此外，还会有相关的饮料机会供我们把握。

This brings us to a final reality check for our business plan. We will, once more, think in reverse like Jacobi. What must we avoid because we don’t want it? Four answers seem clear:

这就引出了对我们商业计划的最后一次现实检验。我们将再次像雅各比那样反向思考。因为不想要，我们必须避开什么？四个答案似乎很明确：

First, we must avoid the protective, cloying, stop-consumption effects of aftertaste that are a standard part of physiology, developed through Darwinian evolution to enhance the replication of man’s genes by forcing a generally helpful moderation on the gene carrier. To serve our ends, on hot days, a consumer must be able to drink container after container of our product with almost no impediment from aftertaste. We will find a wonderful no-aftertaste flavor by trial and error and will thereby solve this problem.

第一，我们必须避开余味那种保护性的、令人腻烦的、阻止继续消费的作用——这是生理学标准的一部分，它是通过达尔文式进化发展出来的，通过对基因载体施加一般有益的节制，来促进人类基因的复制。为了达到我们的目的，在炎热的日子里，消费者必须能够一个接一个地喝下我们的产品，几乎不受余味的阻碍。我们将通过反复试验找到一种绝妙的无余味风味，从而解决这个问题。

Second, we must avoid ever losing even half of our powerful trademarked name. It will cost us mightily, for instance, if our sloppiness should ever allow the sale of any other kind of “cola,” for instance a “Peppy Cola.” If there is ever a Peppy Cola, we will be the proprietor of the brand.

第二，我们必须避免哪怕失去一半我们那强大的商标名称。例如，如果我们的疏忽竟让任何其他种类的「可乐」——比如一种「佩皮可乐」（Peppy Cola）——得以销售，我们将付出惨重代价。如果出现了佩皮可乐，那我们就要成为这个品牌的所有者。

“It will cost us mightily if our sloppiness should ever allow the sale of any other kind of ‘cola,’ for instance a ‘Peppy Cola.‘”倘若我们的马虎，竟放任任何其他『可乐』——比如『噼啪可乐』（Peppy Cola）——被卖掉，那代价将极为惨重。

Third, with so much success coming, we must avoid bad effects from envy, which is given a prominent place in the Ten Commandments because envy is so much a part of human nature. The best way to avoid envy, as recognized by Aristotle,225Aristotle(384–322 BC), born at Stagira, a Greek colony, was son to a court physician for the king of Macedonia. Joining the Academy in Athens, Aristotle studied under Plato for 20 years. Diverging from Plato’s teaching, Aristotle ultimately established his own school, the Lyceum. Following Alexander’s death and the overthrow of his government, Aristotle faced charges of impiety and was forced to flee. He died exiled from Athens. Aristotle’s works include treatises on physics, metaphysics, rhetoric, and ethics. He is also known for his observations about nature and the physical world, which formed the basis for the modern study of biology.亚里士多德（Aristotle，公元前 384–前 322 年）生于斯塔基拉——一个希腊殖民地，是马其顿国王御医之子。进入雅典的学园后，亚里士多德师从柏拉图长达 20 年。在与柏拉图的教学分道扬镳后，亚里士多德最终创办了自己的学校——吕克昂学园。亚历山大大帝去世、其政府被推翻后，亚里士多德面临不敬神的指控，被迫逃离，客死雅典之外。亚里士多德的著作涵盖物理学、形而上学、修辞学和伦理学的论著。他也以对自然和物质世界的观察闻名，这些观察构成了现代生物学研究的基础。 is to plainly deserve the success we get. We will be fanatic about product quality, quality of product presentation, and reasonableness of prices, considering the harmless pleasure we will provide.

第三，随着如此巨大的成功到来，我们必须避开嫉妒带来的恶劣影响——嫉妒在《十诫》中占据显著位置，因为它是人性中如此根深蒂固的一部分。正如亚里士多德225Aristotle(384–322 BC), born at Stagira, a Greek colony, was son to a court physician for the king of Macedonia. Joining the Academy in Athens, Aristotle studied under Plato for 20 years. Diverging from Plato’s teaching, Aristotle ultimately established his own school, the Lyceum. Following Alexander’s death and the overthrow of his government, Aristotle faced charges of impiety and was forced to flee. He died exiled from Athens. Aristotle’s works include treatises on physics, metaphysics, rhetoric, and ethics. He is also known for his observations about nature and the physical world, which formed the basis for the modern study of biology.亚里士多德（Aristotle，公元前 384–前 322 年）生于斯塔基拉——一个希腊殖民地，是马其顿国王御医之子。进入雅典的学园后，亚里士多德师从柏拉图长达 20 年。在与柏拉图的教学分道扬镳后，亚里士多德最终创办了自己的学校——吕克昂学园。亚历山大大帝去世、其政府被推翻后，亚里士多德面临不敬神的指控，被迫逃离，客死雅典之外。亚里士多德的著作涵盖物理学、形而上学、修辞学和伦理学的论著。他也以对自然和物质世界的观察闻名，这些观察构成了现代生物学研究的基础。（Aristotle）所认识到的，避免嫉妒的最佳方式是：理所应当地配得上我们所获得的成功。考虑到我们将提供的无害快乐，我们将狂热地追求产品质量、产品呈现的质量，以及价格的合理性。

fig 226

The Ten Commandments
“With so much success coming, we must avoid bad effects from envy, which is given a prominent place in the Ten Commandments because envy is so much a part of human nature.”既然巨大的成功在望，我们必须避开妒忌带来的恶果——《十诫》给妒忌留了显要位置，正因它如此深植人性。

Fourth, after our trademarked flavor dominates our new market, we must avoid making any huge and sudden change in our flavor.228New Coke新可乐 Even if a new flavor performs better in blind taste tests, changing to that new flavor would be a foolish thing to do. This follows because, under such conditions, our old flavor will be so entrenched in consumer preference by psychological effects that a big flavor change would do us little good, and it would do immense harm by triggering in consumers the standard deprival-superreaction syndrome that makes “take-aways” so hard to get in any type of negotiation and helps make most gamblers so irrational. Moreover, such a large flavor change would allow a competitor, by copying our old flavor, to take advantage of both 1) the hostile consumer superreaction to deprival and 2) the huge love of our original flavor created by our previous work.

第四，在我们的商标风味主宰新市场之后，我们必须避免对风味做任何巨大而突然的改变。即便一种新风味在盲测中表现更好，换成那种新风味也是愚蠢之举。原因在于：在这种条件下，我们的旧风味会由于心理效应而在消费者偏好中如此根深蒂固，以至于大幅改变风味对我们好处甚微，却会因在消费者中触发标准的「剥夺超级反应综合征」而造成巨大伤害——这种综合征使得在任何类型的谈判中「被拿走」都极难接受，并助长了大多数赌徒的非理性。此外，如此大幅的风味改变，会让竞争对手通过复制我们的旧风味而同时利用两点：一、消费者对剥夺的敌对式超级反应；二、我们此前的工作所创造出的对原味的巨大喜爱。

Well, that is my solution to my own problem of turning $2 million into $2 trillion even after paying out billions of dollars in dividends. I think it would have won with Glotz in 1884 and should convince you more than you expected at the outset. After all, the correct strategies are clear after being related to elementary academic ideas brought into play by the helpful notions.

好吧，这就是我对自己的那个问题的解决方案：即便在派发了数十亿美元的股息之后，仍把200万美元变成2万亿美元。我认为它在1884年能赢得格罗兹的认可，而且应当比你们起初预期的更有说服力。毕竟，一旦把这些有用的观念所调动起来的基础学术观念联系起来，正确的策略就一目了然了。

How consistent is my solution with the history of the real Coca-Cola Company229Coca-cola stock可口可乐股票? Well, as late as 1896, 12 years after the fictional Glotz was to start vigorously with $2 million in 1884 dollars, the real Coca-Cola Company had a net worth under $150,000 and earnings of about zero. And thereafter, the real Coca-Cola Company did lose half its trademark and did grant perpetual bottling franchises at fixed syrup prices. And some of the bottlers were not very effective and couldn’t easily be changed. And the real Coca-Cola Company, with this system, did lose much pricing control that would have improved results, had it been retained.

我的解决方案与真实可口可乐公司的历史有多吻合？嗯，迟至1896年——也就是虚构的格罗兹本该在1884年用200万美元（1884年币值）大干一场之后的12年——真实的可口可乐公司净资产不足15万美元，盈利接近于零。此后，真实的可口可乐公司确实失去了一半商标，也确实以固定的糖浆价格授予了永久装瓶特许权。其中一些装瓶商效率不高，也难以轻易更换。而真实的可口可乐公司，凭借这套体系，确实丧失了大量本可改善业绩的定价权——如果它保留这些权力的话。

Yet, even so, the real Coca-Cola Company followed so much of the plan given to Glotz that it is now worth about $125 billion and will have to increase its value at only 8 percent per year until 2034 to reach a value of $2 trillion. And it can hit an annual physical volume target of 2.92 trillion servings if servings grow until 2034 at only 6 percent per year, a result consistent with much past experience and leaving plenty of plain-water ingestion for Coca-Cola to replace after 2034. So I would guess that the fictional Glotz, starting earlier and stronger and avoiding the worst errors, would have easily hit his $2 trillion target. And he would have done it well before 2034.

然而，即便如此，真实的可口可乐公司是如此忠实地遵循了给格罗兹的那套计划，以至于它如今价值约1250亿美元，并且只需到2034年之前每年增值8%，就能达到2万亿美元的价值。而如果销量到2034年之前每年仅增长6%，它就能实现每年2.92万亿份的物理销量目标——这一结果与许多过往经验一致，并且还为2034年之后可口可乐替代大量白开水留下了充足空间。因此我猜想，那位虚构的格罗兹，既然起步更早、根基更牢，又避开了最糟糕的错误，理应能轻松击中他那2万亿美元的目标。而且他会在2034年之前很久就做到。

This brings me, at last, to the main purpose of my talk. Large educational implications exist, if my answer to Glotz’s problem is roughly right and if you make one more assumption I believe true—that most PhD educators, even psychology professors and business school deans, would not have given the same simple answer I did. And if I am right in these two ways, this would indicate that our civilization now keeps in place a great many educators who can’t satisfactorily explain Coca-Cola, even in retrospect, and even after watching it closely all their lives. This is not a satisfactory state of affairs.

这终于把我引向了本次演讲的主要目的。如果我对格罗兹问题的回答大体正确，并且如果你再接受一个我相信为真的假设——即大多数拥有博士学位的教育者，甚至心理学教授和商学院院长，都不会给出像我这样简单的答案——那么就存在重大的教育意义。如果我在这两方面都是对的，那就表明，我们的文明如今留用了大量无法令人满意地解释可口可乐的教育者，哪怕是从后见之明，哪怕他们一生都在密切注视着它。这可不是一种令人满意的状况。

我们的文明如今留用了大量无法令人满意地解释可口可乐的教育者，哪怕是从后见之明，哪怕他们一生都在密切注视着它。

“Our civilization now keeps in place a great many educators who can’t satisfactorily explain Coca-Cola, even in retrospect, and even after watching it closely all their lives.”我们的文明如今养着一大批教育人士，他们连可口可乐都解释不清——哪怕事后回想，哪怕一辈子都在近距离观察它。

Moreover—and this result is even more extreme—the brilliant and effective executives who, surrounded by business school and law school graduates, have run the Coca-Cola Company with glorious success in recent years also did not understand elementary psychology well enough to predict and avoid the New Coke fiasco, which dangerously threatened their company. That people so talented, surrounded by professional advisers from the best universities, should thus demonstrate a huge gap in their education is also not a satisfactory state of affairs.

此外——而且这个结果更加极端——那些才华横溢、行事高效的经理人，周围环绕着商学院和法学院的毕业生，近年来把可口可乐公司经营得极为成功，但他们同样没有足够理解基础心理学，以致无法预测并避开「新可乐228New Coke新可乐」（New Coke）那场几乎危及公司的惨败。如此才华横溢的人，身边还围着来自顶尖大学的职业顾问，却在教育上显露出如此巨大的缺口，这同样不是一种令人满意的状况。

Such extreme ignorance, in both the high reaches of academia and the high reaches of business, is a lollapalooza effect of a negative sort, demonstrating grave defects in academia. Because the bad effect is a lollapalooza, we should expect to find intertwined, multiple academic causes. I suspect at least two such causes:

学术界高层与企业高层中这种极度的无知，是一种负面类型的 lollapalooza 效应，暴露出学术界的严重缺陷。因为这种坏效应是一个 lollapalooza 效应，我们就应当预期能找到相互交织的、多重学术成因。我怀疑至少有这样两个成因。

First, academic psychology, while it is admirable and useful as a list of ingenious and important experiments, lacks intradisciplinary synthesis. In particular, not enough attention is given to lollapalooza effects coming from combinations of psychological tendencies. This creates a situation reminding one of a rustic teacher who tries to simplify schoolwork by rounding pi to an even 3. And it violates Einstein’s230Albert Einstein injunction that “everything should be made as simple as possible, but no more simple.” In general, psychology is laid out and misunderstood, as electromagnetism would now be misunderstood if physics had produced many brilliant experimenters like Michael Faraday231Michael FaradayMichael Faraday (1791–1867) , the child of a blacksmith in England, was apprenticed at age 14 to a bookbinder and bookseller. He became a voracious reader, and his bookbinding duties also led him to the study of chemistry, at which he excelled. He discovered benzene and was the first to describe the compounds of chlorine and carbon. He also experimented with magnetism and electricity, leading him to produce continuous rotation using electric current—a necessary precursor to the electric motor. Faraday is also credited with the discovery of electromagnetic induction, principles of electrolysis, and a method to measure electrical charges, the voltameter.迈克尔·法拉第（Michael Faraday，1791–1867 年）是英格兰一位铁匠之子，14 岁被送去给一位书籍装订商兼书商当学徒。他如饥似渴地阅读，装订书籍的工作也把他引向了化学，而他在化学上表现优异。他发现了苯，最先描述了氯和碳的化合物。他还实验磁学和电学，从而用电流产生了连续旋转——这是电动机的必要先声。法拉第还因发现电磁感应、电解原理，以及一种测量电荷的方法（电量计）而载入史册。 and no grand synthesizer like James Clerk Maxwell.232James Clerk MaxwellJames Clerk Maxwell (1831–1879) , born in Edinburgh, Scotland, demonstrated a very early interest in optics; a favorite childhood pastime of his was using a mirror to reflect the sun’s rays. His unusual mode of dress earned him the nickname “Dafty” at Edinburgh Academy. Nonetheless, he was a brilliant student, excelling in mathematics. He attended Cambridge University and joined its staff of lecturers following graduation. His interest in optics led him to study colors and astronomy. He also made significant contributions in the field of electromagnetism, including the first proposal that light is a form of electromagnetic radiation.詹姆斯·克拉克·麦克斯韦（James Clerk Maxwell，1831–1879 年）生于苏格兰爱丁堡，很小就对光学表现出兴趣，儿时最喜欢的消遣是用镜子反射太阳光。他奇特的穿着为他赢得了“达夫蒂”（Dafty）的绰号。尽管如此，他仍是个出色的学生，数学尤为突出。他进入剑桥大学，毕业后留校任教。对光学的兴趣引导他研究色彩和天文学。他还在电磁学领域作出了重大贡献，包括首次提出光是一种电磁辐射。

学院派心理学，尽管作为一系列巧妙而重要的实验清单值得钦佩且有用，却缺乏学科内部综合。

Einstein, Faraday, and Maxwell

Second, there is a truly horrible lack of synthesis blending psychology and other academic subjects. But only an interdisciplinary approach will correctly deal with reality—in academia as with the Coca-Cola Company.234The University of Chicago芝加哥大学

第二，心理学与其他学科之间确实严重缺乏融合。但只有跨学科的方法才能正确地应对现实——无论对学术界，还是对可口可乐公司，皆如此。

In short, academic psychology departments are immensely more important and useful than other academic departments think. And at the same time, the psychology departments are immensely worse than most of their inhabitants think. It is, of course, normal for self-appraisal to be more positive than external appraisal. Indeed, a problem of this sort may have given you your speaker today. But the size of this psychology department gap is preposterously large. In fact, the gap is so enormous that one very eminent university, Chicago, simply abolished its psychology department, perhaps with an undisclosed hope of later creating a better version.

简而言之，学院派心理学系远比其他院系所认为的更重要、更有用。与此同时，心理学系却又远比其大多数成员所认为的要糟得多。当然，自我评价比外部评价更积极是正常现象。事实上，这类问题说不定正是今天站在你们面前的这位演讲者的写照。但这个心理学系的落差之大，荒谬到了极点。事实上，这个鸿沟如此巨大，以至于有一所非常知名的大学——芝加哥大学234The University of Chicago芝加哥大学（University of Chicago）——干脆取消了它的心理学系，也许是暗自希望日后能建立一个更好的版本。

学院派心理学系远比其他院系所认为的更重要、更有用。与此同时，心理学系却又远比其大多数成员所认为的要糟得多。

“Academic psychology departments are immensely more important and useful than other academic departments think. And at the same time, the psychology departments are immensely worse than most of their inhabitants think.”心理学系远比其他科系所认为的更为重要、有用。与此同时，心理学系又远比它大多数学者所认为的糟糕得多。

In such a state of affairs, many years ago and with much that was plainly wrong already present, the New Coke fiasco occurred. Therein, Coke’s executives came to the brink of destroying the most valuable trademark in the world. The academically correct reaction to this immense and well-publicized fiasco would have been the sort of reaction Boeing would display if three of its new airplanes crashed in a single week. After all, product integrity is involved in each case, and the plain educational failure was immense.

在这样的状况下，多年前，在诸多明显错误的因素已经存在的情况下，发生了「新可乐」惨败。在那场惨败中，可口可乐的高管们走到了毁掉全世界最有价值商标的边缘。学术界对这场巨大且广为宣扬的失败本该有的正确反应，应当类似于波音（Boeing）公司在一周内三架新飞机坠毁时所能展现的反应。毕竟，两种情形都涉及产品完整性，而其中昭然若揭的教育失败都是巨大的。

But almost no such responsible Boeing-like reaction has come from academia. Instead, academia, by and large, continues in its balkanized way to tolerate psychology professors who misteach psychology, non-psychology professors who fail to consider psychological effects obviously crucial in their subject matter, and professional schools that carefully preserve psychological ignorance coming in with each entering class and are proud of their inadequacies.

但学术界几乎没有给出这种负责任的、波音式的反应。相反，学术界大体上继续以它那割裂的方式，容忍着错误地教授心理学的心理学教授、不去考虑其学科中明显关键的心理效应的非心理学教授，以及那些小心翼翼地保留着每一届新生带来的心理无知、并以其不足为荣的专业学院。

Even though this regrettable blindness and lassitude is now the normal academic result, are there exceptions providing hope that disgraceful shortcomings of the education establishment will eventually be corrected? Here, my answer is a very optimistic yes.

尽管这种令人遗憾的盲目与懈怠如今已是学术界的常态，但是否存在一些例外，能让我们看到教育体制那些可耻的缺陷终将被纠正的希望呢？对此，我的答案是一个非常乐观的「有」。

For instance, consider the recent behavior of the economics department of the University of Chicago. Over the last decade, this department has enjoyed a near monopoly of the Nobel Prizes in economics, largely by getting good predictions out of free-market models postulating man’s rationality. And what is the reaction of this department after winning so steadily with its rational-man approach? Well, it has just invited into a precious slot amid its company of greats a wise and witty Cornell economist, Richard Thaler.235Richard ThalerRichard Thaler (b. 1945), born in New Jersey, earned his PhD at the University of Rochester. Serving professorships at Cornell and MIT in behavioral economics and decision research, he joined the faculty at University of Chicago in 1995. In addition to his work on behavioral economics and finance, he focuses on the psychology of decision-making.理查德·塞勒（Richard Thaler，1945 年生）生于新泽西，在罗切斯特大学获得博士学位。他先后在康奈尔大学和麻省理工学院担任行为经济学与决策研究的教职，1995 年加入芝加哥大学教师队伍。除了行为经济学和金融学的工作，他还专注于决策心理学。 And it has done this because Thaler pokes fun at much that is holy at the University of Chicago. Indeed, Thaler believes, with me, that people are often massively irrational in ways predicted by psychology that must be taken into account in microeconomics.

例如，看看芝加哥大学234The University of Chicago芝加哥大学（University of Chicago）经济学系近来的举动。在过去十年里，该系几乎垄断了诺贝尔经济学奖，很大程度上是靠着「自由市场」模型——它假定人是理性的——得出了良好的预测。那么，这个系在凭借理性人方法如此稳定地连连获胜之后，作何反应呢？嗯，它刚刚在群贤之中一个宝贵的席位上，邀请了一位睿智而诙谐的康奈尔大学（Cornell）经济学家理查德·泰勒（Richard Thaler）。它这么做，是因为泰勒对芝加哥大学奉为神圣的许多东西大加调侃。事实上，泰勒和我都相信，人们常常以心理学所能预测的方式极度非理性，而这一点在微观经济学中必须被纳入考量。

人们常常以心理学所能预测的方式极度非理性，而这一点在微观经济学中必须被纳入考量。

“People are often massively irrational in ways predicted by psychology that must be taken into account in microeconomics.”人们常常以一种心理学可预测的、极度不理性的方式行事，而这必须被微观经济学纳入考量。

In so behaving, the University of Chicago is imitating Darwin, who spent much of his long life thinking in reverse as he tried to disprove his own hardest-won and best-loved ideas. And so long as there are parts of academia that keep alive its best values by thinking in reverse like Darwin, we can confidently expect that silly educational practices will eventually be replaced by better ones, exactly as Carl Jacobi might have predicted.

芝加哥大学这样的举动，是在效仿达尔文（Darwin），后者在其漫长的生命中，花了大量时间进行反向思考，试图证伪他自己来之不易、最为珍爱的那些观念。只要学术界中还有部分人像达尔文那样通过反向思考保持其最优秀的价值观，我们就能满怀信心地期待，那些愚蠢的教育做法终将被更好的做法取代，正如卡尔·雅各比可能会预测的那样。

This will happen because the Darwinian approach, with its habitual objectivity taken on as a sort of hair shirt, is a mighty approach indeed. No less a figure than Einstein said that one of the four causes of his achievement was self-criticism, ranking right up there alongside curiosity, concentration, and perseverance.

这会发生，因为达尔文式的方法——把习惯性的客观当作一种苦修——确实是一种强大的方法。连爱因斯坦（Einstein）这样的人物都说过，他成就的四大成因之一便是自我批评，它与好奇心、专注和毅力并列。

And, to further appreciate the power of self-criticism, consider where lies the grave of that very “ungifted” undergraduate, Charles Darwin. It is in Westminster Abbey, right next to the headstone of Isaac Newton,236Isaac NewtonAt birth in Lincolnshire, England, Isaac Newton (1642–1727) was so tiny and frail that he was not expected to live. Yet he lived into his 80s. During his young adulthood, Newton made tremendous discoveries in general mathematics, algebra, geometry, calculus, optics, and celestial mechanics. Most famous among these discoveries was his description of gravity. The publication of his book The Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy in 1687 marked the peak of Newton’s creative career.艾萨克·牛顿（Isaac Newton，1642–1727 年）生于英格兰林肯郡，出生时瘦小孱弱，人们以为他活不下来。然而他一直活到八十多岁。青年时期，牛顿在普通数学、代数、几何、微积分、光学和天体力学上都取得了巨大发现，其中最著名的是他对万有引力的描述。1687 年他的著作《自然哲学的数学原理》（The Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy）出版，标志着他创造生涯的巅峰。 perhaps the most gifted student who ever lived, honored on that headstone in eight Latin words constituting the most eloquent praise in all graveyard print: “Hic depositum est, quod mortale fuit Isaaci Newtoni”—“Here lies that which was mortal of Isaac Newton.”

而为了进一步领会自我批评的力量，不妨想想那位「天资平平」的本科生查尔斯·达尔文（Charles Darwin）的坟墓在哪里。它就在威斯敏斯特教堂（Westminster Abbey），紧挨着艾萨克·牛顿236Isaac NewtonAt birth in Lincolnshire, England, Isaac Newton (1642–1727) was so tiny and frail that he was not expected to live. Yet he lived into his 80s. During his young adulthood, Newton made tremendous discoveries in general mathematics, algebra, geometry, calculus, optics, and celestial mechanics. Most famous among these discoveries was his description of gravity. The publication of his book The Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy in 1687 marked the peak of Newton’s creative career.艾萨克·牛顿（Isaac Newton，1642–1727 年）生于英格兰林肯郡，出生时瘦小孱弱，人们以为他活不下来。然而他一直活到八十多岁。青年时期，牛顿在普通数学、代数、几何、微积分、光学和天体力学上都取得了巨大发现，其中最著名的是他对万有引力的描述。1687 年他的著作《自然哲学的数学原理》（The Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy）出版，标志着他创造生涯的巅峰。（Isaac Newton）的墓碑——牛顿也许是有史以来天资最出众的学生——墓碑上那八个拉丁词，构成了墓碑文字中最雄辩的赞辞：「Hic depositum est, quod mortale fuit Isaaci Newtoni」；「此处长眠着艾萨克·牛顿那终有一死之躯。」

A civilization that so places a dead Darwin will eventually develop and integrate psychology in a proper and practical fashion that greatly increases skills of all sorts. But all of us who have dollops of power and see the light should help the process along. There is a lot at stake. If, in many high places, a universal product as successful as Coca-Cola is not properly understood and explained, it can’t bode well for our competency in dealing with much else that is important.

一个如此安放逝去达尔文的文明，终将以恰当而务实的方式发展并整合心理学，从而极大地提升各类技能。但我们所有拥有些许权力并看清这一点的人，都应当推动这一进程。此事关系重大。如果在许多高层位上，像可口可乐这样成功的普世产品都得不到恰当的理解与解释，那对于我们应对其他许多重要事务的能力，便不会是什么好兆头。

Of course, those of you with 50 percent of net worth in Coca-Cola stock, occurring because you tried to invest 10 percent after thinking like I did in making my pitch to Glotz, can ignore my message about psychology as too elementary for useful transmission to you. But I am not so sure that this reaction is wise for the rest of you. The situation reminds me of the old-time Warner & Swasey237Warner & Swasey华纳-斯韦西公司 ad that was a favorite of mine: “The company that needs a new machine tool and hasn’t bought it is already paying for it.”

当然，你们中那些把净资产50%都投在可口可乐股票229Coca-cola stock可口可乐股票上的人——之所以如此，是因为你们在像我向格罗兹陈词那样思考之后，本想投资10%——可以把我关于心理学的这番话当作太基础、对你们已无传授价值而置之不理。但我并不那么确信，对你们其余的人而言，这种反应是明智的。这种情形让我想起华纳及史瓦塞（Warner & Swasey）公司那句我很喜欢的旧广告：「需要新机床却没有购买的公司，其实已经在为它付钱了。」

需要新机床却没有购买的公司，其实已经在为它付钱了。
